title: Morphogenetic goal-directedness smooths the fitness landscape and boosts evolvability

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Morphogenetic goal-directedness smooths the fitness landscape and boosts evolvability

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Morphogenetic goal-directedness is a major evolutionary ratchet: because tissues adjust to reach the same anatomical goals despite changed conditions (e.g. muscle, vessels and tendons building a workable extra finger around an ectopic bone), it hides the disruptive effects of random mutations and smooths the anatomical fitness landscape.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Morphogenetic goal-directedness is a major evolutionary ratchet, smoothing the anatomical fitness landscape by hiding the otherwise potentially disruptive effects of random mutations.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Discussion”. Scope: Evolution of anatomy in organisms with regulative development

fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-23: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.44

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Phenotypic buffering and fitness-landscape smoothing have measurable consequences in public genotype-phenotype resources. Existing datasets can test subsets, but attributing the effect specifically to morphogenetic goal-directedness and calling it a major ratchet are broader than current coverage.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For developmental perturbations and mutations, quantify anatomical variance and fitness with intact versus impaired regulative responses, then test whether regulation reduces phenotypic effect sizes and increases viable mutational neighborhoods.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Datasets rarely measure regulation, anatomy, and fitness together.

Goal-directedness is not uniquely separated from developmental robustness.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Robustness of anatomy to mutation is a definable contrast between regulative and non-regulative development. The measurements that would populate that contrast, matched mutational neighborhoods of anatomy, have not been released as a dataset. Other sources of canalization predict the same smoothing, so even a future landscape would need the with-versus-without set-point arm. Existing anecdotes do not resolve the ratchet.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare anatomical viability under the same mutational perturbations in lineages or models with regulative, set-point development and in matched systems without it. Smoothing is confirmed if goal-directed development yields more viable neighbor phenotypes; equal fragility would refute a ratchet that hides mutational disruption.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No public anatomical fitness landscape is paired with a measured morphogenetic set point.

Canalization from gene-network structure produces the same smoothing.

The extra-digit anecdote is not a dataset.
